the radiobiological principles that underlie radiation protection standards are based on epidemiologic studies, which have demonstrated that the risk of cancer induction increases linearly with dose, and that the risk per unit dose is about the same for all organs and tissues.
radiation protection standards are based on radiobiological principles, and that the new ICRP and NCRP recommendations are consistent with the current state of the art.

the radiobiological principles of radiation protection are based on a solid foundation of published results from the effects of radiation on humans and experimental animals, and that the new findings have been incorporated into the latest radiation protection recommendations.

the radiobiological principles of radiation protection are the foundation for the development of the radiation protection standards and recommendations, which are based on the results of epidemiological studies and on experimental data in animals, including data on the effects of radiation on the developing embryo and the fetus.

we have reviewed the radiobiological principles of radiation protection and have analyzed the published results of effects of ionizing radiations at the cellular level in animal experiments and epidemiological studies, as well as human data on cancer, including increases on the risk of second cancer following radiation therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the radiation protection guidelines are based on the best current understanding of the effects of radiation, and that the guidelines are being continuously updated as new information becomes available.
radiation protection standards, as currently formulated, are not sufficiently stringent for the protection of patients and staff in radiotherapy.

the new ICRP and NCRP recommendations, based on the most up‐to‐date epidemiological data on radiation induced cancers and tissue reactions, will lead to a significant increase in the dose limits and dose constraints for the general public and for radiation workers, as well as for patients undergoing medical procedures.
